narrative.overview: A tool for reading probabilities, built so the numbers never have to compete with the page. Pale cool ground, soft black ink, one serif italic voice raised for headings and a few large numerals. Brimble's ground and type meet Practice Gateway's pill navigation, pill buttons, rounded cards and one dark night screen.
keyCharacteristics: Pale ground, soft black ink, one blue that means data and nothing else.
Lora italic for display voice; IBM Plex Sans for everything read; IBM Plex Mono only for fair odds.
Floating white pill navigation; pill buttons; 16px white cards; 24px night panels.
One dark navy screen (the track record) set against the light ones.
Motion is rare and once-only, and switches off with the browser's reduce-motion setting.

rules.name: The Blue Is Data Rule
rules.body: Blue marks data and interactive things only; never to say a prediction is good or bad.

rules.name: The Logo-Only Warm Rule
rules.body: Orange and red appear in the logo mark and nowhere else.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif italic is for headings and the large probability numerals only.

rules.name: The Solid Float Rule
rules.body: The floating navigation is opaque white. No glass, no blur.

dos: Do put a plain-words label next to every bar, number and tag; colour never carries meaning alone.
Do keep Signal Blue for data and interactive elements only.
Do keep motion once-only and turn all of it off for reduce-motion.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better.
donts: Don't use red or green, or the logo's warm colours, to signal good or bad predictions.
Don't animate probabilities while they are being read.
Don't make the floating navigation translucent.
Don't set body text, buttons or table cells in the serif italic.
Don't add small uppercase labels above headings.
